themes.name: AI compute: NVIDIA's supply chain
themes.what: The AI selloff paused on Oct 15. The Nasdaq closed up 0.1% at 26,713.02 after falling more than 1% early. By dashboard closes CoreWeave rose 5.9% to 69.69 after Nvidia's Jensen Huang said it needs no Nvidia backstop, Oracle rose 3.0% to 134.47 and Micron 1.9% to 931.24, while Nvidia fell 1.8% to 217.23 and the TSMC ADR 1.8% to 422.25. In Europe ASM International fell about 7% and Infineon about 5%. HPE fell about 7% on Oct 14 after Barclays cut it to Equal Weight, citing weak AI driven growth.
themes.for_you: No action. One up day is not a turn: NVDA (up/down volume 0.98) and ANET (0.90) slipped to 'Buy zone, wait for the chart'. CRWV, ORCL and MU are left out of both lists because they bounced on a day their credit and memory worries did not change. HPE is a scanner put candidate on Setups; the downgrade is why its premium is rich.

themes.name: AI power and the grid
themes.what: Venture Global signed frame agreements with GE Vernova and Baker Hughes for up to 16 gas fired power island units of 720 MW each, plus transformers, to support up to 10 GW of data center compute by 2034. If every order goes ahead the bill is about $17.2 billion (8-K); the first order is planned by the end of 2026 and first power in late 2028 or early 2029. Off grid gas keeps winning because the grid queue is too slow.
themes.for_you: GEV is 'Buy zone now' (926.44 on Oct 15, zone 904.03 to 994.38, up/down volume 1.25), so a small long term tranche fits. This is a frame deal, not firm orders. BKR is rated Avoid. No swing setup.

themes.name: Critical materials and geopolitics
themes.what: Alcoa reported Q3 on Oct 15: adjusted EPS $1.82, revenue $3.7 billion (down from $3.97 billion in Q2 on lower metal prices), free cash flow $472 million, alumina output up 11% to 2.5 million tons, and the Alumar smelter in Brazil fully restarted. South32 holders approved the AliGroup deal, which Alcoa expects to close in the first half of 2027.
themes.for_you: No action. AA has no dashboard verdict (Not enough data) and is down 12.6% in a month with up/down volume 0.79. Strong cash and higher output against falling metal prices cut both ways, so it is in neither list.

themes.name: Fintech and Crypto Rails: Stablecoins, Tokenization, Exchanges
themes.what: Interactive Brokers reported Q3 on Oct 15: accounts up 35% to 5.58 million, customer equity up 27% to $964.7 billion, margin loans up 36% to $105.2 billion, and the quarterly dividend raised to $0.15 from $0.0875. Separately the SEC approved Cboe binary options tied to company metrics (Chair Atkins, Oct 13), covering more than 100 metrics at 23 companies; Robinhood is expected to offer them first, with no launch date set.
themes.for_you: CBOE rose 2.5% to 308.09 on Oct 15, above its 278.34 to 296.41 zone, so it moved to 'Accumulate on pullback': wait for a dip. HOOD is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' (up/down volume 0.94). Record margin loans at brokers mean forced selling can come fast if tech breaks again. COIN is a listed company in the new contracts but has no verdict, so it is left out.

themes.name: Healthcare and Medtech: Aging, Heart, Sugar, Hearing, Sight
themes.what: Health care led the S&P 500 again on Oct 15, up 1.8% and 4.3% over two sessions (TheStreet), and the big health care ETF hit an intraday record. By dashboard closes LLY rose 3.5% to 1,251.61 on 1.55x volume, MDT 1.3% to 95.45 on 2.8x volume and PFE 0.8% to 29.44. All three are now above their buy zones, so their verdicts moved from 'Buy zone now' to 'Accumulate on pullback'. No trial result or approval drove it; it is money leaving tech.
themes.for_you: Long term: do not chase. Wait for pullbacks toward the zone tops: LLY 1,214.21, MDT 92.90, PFE 28.74. Swing: PFE is a setup (entry 29.95, needs 50.6M+ shares). The PFE $27 put idea is dropped today.

innovations.name: Communications
innovations.what: Rechecked on the daily rotation. Ericsson's Q3 (Oct 15) showed sales of SEK 59.5 billion against 56.2 billion a year ago, 7% organic growth led by Networks, and net income down to about SEK 5.8 billion because last year included a divestment gain. It still sees a flat radio market in 2026 and rising AI driven component costs. The ERIC ADR jumped 11.8% to 10.71 on about 4.5 times normal volume. Amazon had almost 400 Leo satellites up as of Oct 9; AST has not yet dated its next launch.
innovations.for_you: No action. ERIC and NOK have no dashboard verdict. A flat radio market keeps AI-RAN at the pilot stage, so the stage does not move. KEYS (342.08) and VIAV (36.82), which test these networks, are 'Buy zone now' but fell 4.3% and 4.5% on Oct 15, so they are left out of the bullish list until the selling stops.

countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: The runoff is tightening. Quaest (Oct 10 to 13, 2,154 people, released Oct 14) has Flavio Bolsonaro at 51% of valid votes to Lula's 49%, and O Povo reports Datafolha (Oct 13 to 15) at the same 51% to 49%, down from 52% to 48% earlier and inside the 2 point margin of error. EWZ fell 2.4% to 41.58 on Oct 15.
countries.for_you: Brazilian banks rallied on a Bolsonaro lead that is now inside the margin of error. NU is 'Buy zone now', but wait for the Oct 25 result before acting.

countries.name: China
countries.what: China's September exports rose 36.3% from a year ago (25% in August) and imports about 31%, for a $133.5 billion monthly surplus; chip exports rose 108.1% and exports to the US 39.6% (released Oct 14). The nine month surplus is about $938 billion, which adds to EU and US pressure to rebalance trade.
countries.for_you: No action. Rising Chinese chip exports support the case against new MU swings. AAPL is left out of both lists: strong Chinese trade helps its supply chain, but a trade fight would hurt it.

countries.name: European Union
countries.what: Ericsson beat on Q3 sales (SEK 59.5 billion, 7% organic growth) and its ADR jumped 11.8% on Oct 15, while European chip stocks fell again: ASM International about 7% and Infineon about 5% (CNBC). AI hardware is under pressure in Europe too, but telecom networks are recovering.
countries.for_you: No action. ERIC has no dashboard verdict. ASML (1,657.44 ADR, up 0.5% on Oct 15) is rated 'Not enough data', so it is left out of both lists.

countries.name: India
countries.what: India's September consumer prices rose 5.54% from a year ago, up from 4.83% in August, with food up 7.74% (MoSPI, Oct 12). Inflation is now above the RBI's own 5.2% forecast, which backs its Oct 7 hike and keeps another one possible.
countries.for_you: No action; nothing here is on your lists. INDA rose 1.9% on Oct 15 but its up/down volume is 0.70, so sellers still lead.

countries.name: Japan
countries.what: The Nikkei rose about 1.4% to 65,324.29 on Oct 16 (AP; Saxo later had +1.8% to 65,584.61) after its 4.9% drop, as Wall Street steadied and Fed Chair Warsh called AI a big plus for growth.
countries.for_you: No action. A partial bounce after a 4.9% fall does not change the chip test names, so they are in neither list. The BOJ meets Oct 30.

countries.name: South Korea
countries.what: The KOSPI bounced on Oct 16 after the 7.57% crash: AP had it up about 2.1% at 5,668.05 early, and Saxo later reported a 4.11% gain to 5,782.62, with Samsung and SK hynix steadying. The close was not confirmed at writing.
countries.for_you: No action. One up day after a 7.6% crash is not a bottom, so EWY and MU are in neither list. Wait for SK hynix (Oct 28) and Samsung (Oct 29) results before any memory trade. EWY closed Oct 15 at 156.22, down 11% in a month.
